en: The *Dhāraṇī-sūtra of Holding the World*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was staying in the kingdom of Kauśāmbī at Kalandaka...
At Kālinjara,
he was accompanied by a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus,
surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable multitude including bodhisattva-mahāsattvas numbering in the millions, as well as devas, humans, asuras, and others.
At that time, there was an elder in that country named Moon of Wondrous Virtue (Candrasena).
His appearance was dignified and radiant, and his character was serene and far-reaching.
He had a great many sons, daughters, male and female servants.
Having conceived deep reverence and faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha,
he approached the Buddha, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, and then withdrew to stand to one side.
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I wish to ask the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, about a few matters of slight doubt.
I only pray that, out of great compassion, you will take pity on me and grant me permission."
At that time, out of compassion for him, the World-Honored One spoke with a voice of loving-kindness and gentleness, saying:
"Householder, ask whatever you wish."
"I shall now employ skillful means to analyze this for you so as to gladden your heart.
At that time, the elder was filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
he prostrated himself in salutation, joined his palms, and requested, saying:
"Bhagavān, how can good sons and good daughters cause those who are poor and lowly to attain wealth and nobility,
and cause those who are ill to be cured of their diseases?"
"May those with transgressions have their offenses extinguished;
may those who are endangered and fearful find peace and happiness.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing [the answer], asked anyway.
"For what reason does the householder make such a request?
Then that householder addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One, we who live at home have many kinsmen and dependents."
Lacking sufficient wealth, it is difficult to provide for everyone;
moreover, we are beset by many ailments and burdened by karmic offenses, living in constant fear and anxiety.
Therefore, we entreat the World-Honored One to reveal the skillful means for our sake.
It causes those who are poor and lowly to obtain great wealth and status;
it provides for their relatives and extensively cultivates acts of charity;
and it increases all storehouses so that they become inexhaustible.
May those who are ill have the four great elements become harmonious and healthy;
may those who diligently cultivate wholesome deeds have neither physical nor mental fatigue;
and may those who have committed offenses swiftly attain their eradication.
Upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy realm;
they will bring peace and happiness to the bodies and minds of those who are distressed and fearful,
and they will draw near to and make offerings to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
"May you swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the elder:
"Good son, in the past, incalculable eons ago, I encountered a Buddha, a World-Honored One."

He is named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Leader of Men to be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān, known as Vajradharasāgaraghoṣa.
For the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings,
he preached a dhāraṇī called "Holding the World.
Upon hearing it, I was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.
By upholding, reciting, and extensively explaining it to others,
one brings benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings;
through these causes and conditions, one’s merit and wisdom will increase.
"May you swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
and preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma for all devas and humans.
Now, for your sake, I shall speak this dhāraṇī."
You gods, humans, and others, all should listen attentively.
Having heard it, you should uphold it and explain it extensively for others.
The power of this divine mantra is inconceivable.
May all sentient beings obtain benefit and happiness.
The dhāraṇī is as follows: Tadyathā.
Sulubhedadharavati-maṅgale.
Añjale añjabhale hagakhani.
Havida-niḥsāpa-ti-dhana-pati.
Dānapati śrīmati prabhāvati.
Amala vimale ruru suḥ.
Lūpā-bi-ma-li-ṛ-nada-nada-sid-ti-vita-sid-ti.
Viśvavāsi śiṅkurale maṅkurale.
Vivi me du dum e tta ttare.
Ṭaḷa ṭaḷa, vañcale vañcale, kaṭe kaṭe, vaṭṭe sanni.
Nirarbuda-patana-paryādaṭa-tathāgata-satyam.
Sakalāni kucam tathāgatānām.
Nusa malarasa malaradharma sacitta malarasaṃgha sacitta ṭaṭa ṭaṭa.
Phu lo phu lo phu ca ya bha lo bha lo.
Nisumbhaghnī śāntā mṛtyupraṇāśinī.
Subhadrapataye āgaccha āgaccha samayam anusmara svāhā.
Apade nāsramala svāhā | Prabhā nāsramala svāhā ||
Dhe-li-lie-zhen-e-nu-sa-mo-lo-sha-ho-bi-zhe-yen.
Anusvāra-lokha svāhā | Sarvasattva-vinayana anusvāra svāhā | This dhāraṇī possesses great supernatural power.
If there are good sons or good daughters [of noble family],...
If one receives and maintains this with a sincere heart and extensively explains it to others,
no evil spirits, ghosts, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans,
non-humans, or the like shall be able to cause them harm.
All matters of benefit and happiness will increase day and night;
if one can sincerely make offerings to the Triple Gem and recite this great dhāraṇī.
For seven days and nights, without a moment's interruption,
all the devas, nāgas, and spirits were filled with joy;
from that time forth, they rained down whatever wealth and grain was required.
Famine and pestilence shall all be eliminated;
all karmic obstructions and hindrances shall be utterly extinguished;
and all perils and fears shall attain peace and security.
"May merit and wisdom gradually increase, may all that is sought be fulfilled as desired,
and may you swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,
bodhi. At that time, the Buddha addressed the elder Candracchattra.
You should have faith in and accept this dhāraṇī;
remember it, recite it, uphold it, and explain it extensively to others.
Whatever benefit and happiness you seek will be fully realized without fail.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
the elder was filled with joy and exultation, and he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I am able to receive and uphold this, and shall explain it extensively for others."
"May you bring benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
We pray only that the World-Honored One will look upon us with compassion and mindfulness.
The World-Honored One replied, "So be it, so be it."
Then that elder, with palms joined in reverence,
circumambulated the World-Honored One a hundred thousand times to the right;
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and departed with joy.
At that time, the World-Honored One said to Ānanda:
"In all the storehouses of the householder Candra,
various kinds of wealth and grain are now completely full."
The Venerable Ānanda, filled with joy, addressed the Buddha:
"By what cause and condition has the householder Candraśrī suddenly found all his treasuries overflowing?"
The Buddha told Ānanda: "When the elder Sucandra hears this great dhāraṇī spoken by me,
he will believe it with deep faith, rejoice, and accept, uphold, read, and recite it."
I pray that you will proclaim it for the sake of immeasurable sentient beings.
By the power of this merit, may all treasuries be filled;
you, too, should uphold, recite, and widely explain this dhāraṇī to others.
May all sentient beings within this trichiliocosm obtain benefit and happiness.
As I observe the world, including its devas, Māras, and Brahmās...
No one is able to destroy or transcend this dhāraṇī,
for its phrases and words are correct, true,
and indestructible; those with meager merit cannot hear it.
Why is this? Because these words and phrases are praised by all Buddhas of the three periods of time,
who empower them with inconceivable spiritual power.
May those who hear and uphold [this] all obtain benefit and happiness.
The Venerable Ānanda, with a heart of deep joy,
praised him in sublime verses, saying:
The Buddhas are inconceivable, and the Dharma they teach is likewise;
those who can correctly practice it will receive a corresponding fruit and retribution.
The King of Dharma, the All-Knowing One, has extinguished birth, old age, sickness, and death.
"Having reached the supreme further shore, I prostrate to the Great Awakened Honored One.
At that time, Ānanda was leaping for joy and, having paid homage to the Buddha with palms joined, addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One..."
"Now, what shall this Dharma-gate be named?
How should we uphold it from now on?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
This is titled "The Questions of the Elder Candracchattra";
it is also titled "That Which Brings About All Wealth and Status," "The Cure for Disease," and "The Extinguisher of Sin."
It is also called that which can eliminate all fear and anxiety;
it is also called that which is praised and extolled by all Buddhas;
it is also called that which is empowered by the spiritual power of all Buddhas.
It is also called the *Dharani-sutra for Sustaining the World*.
You should practice it with devotion and never let it be forgotten or lost,
so as to bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
When the Bhagavat had finished speaking this sutra,
immeasurable śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, along with devas,
humans, asuras, and others, [were filled with joy].
When the entire great assembly heard what the Buddha had spoken,
they were all greatly rejoiced, and with faith and acceptance, they practiced accordingly.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra on Upholding the World*.
